question.prompt: The faces of each of \(7\) standard dice are labeled with the integers from \(1\) to \(6.\) Let \(p\) be the probability that when all \(7\) dice are rolled, the sum of the numbers on the top faces is \(10.\) What other sum occurs with the same probability \(p?\)

solutions.title: Pair opposite faces
solutions.explanation:
Opposite faces of a standard die add to \(7\). Pair each outcome \((x_1,\ldots,x_7)\) with the outcome \((7-x_1,\ldots,7-x_7)\), using the opposite face on every die.

When the original sum is \(10\), the paired sum is
\[
(7-x_1)+\cdots+(7-x_7)=7\cdot7-10=39.
\]
Applying the same pairing again recovers the original outcome. Thus it gives a one-to-one correspondence between outcomes with sum \(10\) and outcomes with sum \(39\). Since all ordered dice outcomes are equally likely, these two sums have the same probability.

The answer is \(\boxed{39}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
